summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, chronic diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and diabetes was admitted for acute respiratory distress following an episode of palpitations and worsening shortness of breath. She had been discharged the prior day after an admission for dialysis-related chest pain and hypotension. This admission was attributed to acute on chronic diastolic heart failure with pulmonary edema, likely triggered by a tachyarrhythmia. She was treated with intravenous nitroglycerin, BiPap support, and hemodialysis with removal of 3.5 liters of fluid. Her heart rate was controlled with rate-limiting medications, and her warfarin dose was temporarily increased due to a low INR. She stabilized on room air, had no further symptoms, and was discharged home with instructions on weight monitoring, fluid and sodium restriction, and continuation of dialysis and medications. Follow-up was arranged through her dialysis clinic for INR monitoring.
